text: I'm 34, and this is advice I would give my 18 years old self. So if in part 1 I said that life is hard and you need to take responsibility for it, and in part 2 I said that you should become independent as early as possible, then part 3 would be this, try different things in life, take risks, and be adventurous. This is very important when you are young, because when you are 18, you often have more time, fewer responsibilities, and more flexibility than you will have later in life. But instead of using that time to explore, many young guys stay in their comfort zone. So what I would tell my younger self is do more things. Study, yes. Work, yes. Build yourself, yes. But also go out, go to parties, travel if you can, socialize, meet new people, try different experiences, build a richer life. And this is especially important when it comes to women. One of the biggest mistakes young guys make, and I was not an exception, is getting obsessed with one girl. You like this girl, and suddenly you start fantasizing, putting her on a pedestal, imagining that she's special or perfect. But how do you even know that? At 18, most guys don't have enough experience to judge properly. You don't really know women yet. You don't even fully know your own standards or whether your standards make sense. And then what happens? The girl doesn't respond that well. Maybe she gives mixed signals. Maybe she friendzones you. Maybe she's not even interested. But instead of moving on, you keep chasing. You start doing all the wrong things you probably learned from movies and TV shows. You try harder, give more attention, invest more emotions, and waste more time. That is exactly what you shouldn't do. If you like a girl, ask her out. If it works, great. If not, move on. Approach and see where it leads you to. To a great story or to a rejection. Either way, you gain experience. That is the path. The only guy who hears no rejections is the guy who does nothing. So if you want to get better with women, you do need to get used to rejections. At the same time, do sports. Sport is the cheapest medicine out there. This should become part of your life. Sports improve your health, your mood, your discipline, your energy, and your appearance. And appearance does matter. Especially in dating. Women notice when a guy looks fit and put together. So try different things and find something you actually enjoy. Gym, martial arts, dancing, team sports, anything. The goal is not just to look better, but to build a stronger lifestyle. Another thing is avoid escapism. Don't spend too much time escaping your real life through video games, endless content, shows, movies, or whatever else becomes your personal addiction. I'm not saying you can never relax. Of course you can. But when every three minutes goes into escape, that usually means your real life is not where it should be. So instead of constantly running away from reality, build a life you don't want to escape from. And finally, try not to compare yourself to random people on social media. You don't know their real life, their background, their struggle, or whether any of it is even real. Compare yourself to yourself in the past. To who you were last month, last year, a few years ago. That is the only person you can reliably compare yourself to. And if you see improvements, even small but steady ones, that is already a huge win. So if I had to summarize part three, it would be this. Take risks. Try things. Don't obsess over one girl. Get experience. Do sports. Avoid escapism. And compare yourself only to your past self. If you can combine this with part one and part two, you will already be moving in a much better direction than most young men out there.
